call_points.text: FY27 capex guidance held at ₹750-900 Cr, with supply chain spend past its peak and new stores the priority.
The 200 bps EBITDA margin expansion target is held, split half Domino's and half emerging brands.
Popeyes LFL growth accelerated to 45% in Q1FY27 from 9.2% in Q1FY26; management gave no normalisation level.
Domino's LFL was 2.5% in Q1FY27 against 11.6% a year earlier, on a high base with price increases taken.
A 200 bps cost headwind was restricted to 20 bps through price increases, waste reduction and efficiency.
LPG alone was a 120 bps hit; cheese, oil and chicken inflation remain in flux with more possible.
Gross margin was 75.5% in Q1FY27 despite the cost headwinds.
The Mumbai food factory was commissioned in March, with some part yet to be commissioned.
Asked for average order value, management declined to share it, saying only that chicken AOVs exceed pizza.
Management expects to add 230 to 250 stores in FY27.
Minimum order value was lowered from ₹149 to ₹99 to drive customer acquisition.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: In FY 2015-16, Revenue Expenditure incurred by the Company but held to be capital in nature by the Assessing Officer (AO) in the assessment orders passed raising a demand of Rs. 23.32 Crs. The issue was decided in favour of the Company by Hon’ble Allahabad High Court in earlier years but Income Tax Department has raised tax demand on same issue in subsequent years and same are pending before CIT(Appeals).
tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company expects to get relief from the Appellate Authority and does not anticipate any material adverse financial implication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received final assessment order dated September 27, 2024 and date of receipt of order is September 30, 2024 for FY 2016-17 raising tax demand of Rs. 70.79 crores on account of certain Transfer Pricing Adjustments.
tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company expects to get relief from the Appellate Authority and does not anticipate any material adverse financial implication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received final assessment order dated October 23, 2024 and date of receipt of order is October 23, 2024 for FY 2020-21, raising tax demand of Rs. 215.97 crores primarily arising on account of mistakes apparent from records apart from certain Transfer Pricing Adjustments and other corporate adjustment. Further, a rectification application is submitted to the Jurisdictional Assessing Officer and pending disposal. The Company expects to get relief from the Assessing Officer.
tax_litigation.status: Update. The Company has received the rectification order whereby the tax demand has been reduced from Rs. 215.97 Crores (original demand - Rs. 216.19 crores) to Rs. 190.21 Crores. The Company continues to believe that the impugned tax demand raised vide aforementioned rectification order has been made ignoring contentions of the Company. The Company has already filed an appeal in the said matter. Post such redressal process, impugned tax demand so raised is likely to get deleted. The Company does not anticipate any material financial implications

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: For FY 2017-18, Appeal Pending before ITAT against Transfer Pricing adjustment raising a demand of Rs. 17 Crs in relation to alleged international transactions in violation of judicial precedents.
tax_litigation.status: No Change The Appellate Authority has remanded the matter back to Assessing Officer to pass the fresh order as per the directions of Dispute Resolution Panel.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has filed Writ Petition before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court against the impugned order passed by National Anti-Profiteering Authority for not passing the benefit of GST to consumers. Hon’ble Delhi High Court has granted interim-stay in the matter. The Company has deposited Rs 20 crores in terms of the directions issued by Hon’ble Delhi High Court.
tax_litigation.status: No change. The Company expects to get relief from the Hon'ble Delhi Court and does not anticipate any material adverse financial implication

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Company has received an Order levying demand of INR 17.12 Crs (including interest – INR 7.68 Crs & Penalty - INR 0.91 Cr) on account of reconciliation issues in GST Input Tax Credit claimed/reversed and GST Output Turnover & Tax Liability in the state of Karnataka.
